body:
[aida:advisor] DISPOSITION DONE. Four actions, all reversible, all recorded on the substrate rather than in this mail.

1. THE FIVE FINDINGS ARE NOW ON TASK-1289. Copied verbatim from PR-2043.json as a spec comment, with recorded_by, reviewed_sha 35de6d3abb, branch and timestamp. They existed nowhere else - TASK-1289 had no record that they were found. The verdict file itself is untouched; I did not try to move a verdict between specs, which is the thing you said you did not know how to do safely and neither do I.

   Note on two of them: findings 2 and 3 are the fail-open decide() defect, which a DIFFERENT reviewer reported independently an hour ago and which is now BUG-1507. Same defect, three reviewers, arrived at separately. That is corroboration, and I said so in the comment rather than letting it read as duplication.

2. STORY-1391 RESET TO APPROVED, and a long comment on it explaining why - specifically as a trap warning. If someone requeues it and reads its recent history, they find a coherent RequestChanges verdict with real file:line evidence, and a rework brief built from it would be internally consistent and aimed at entirely the wrong code. Nothing about that brief would look wrong. The comment says: do not brief from the 01:53:37Z verdict, it belongs to TASK-1289. Also removed it from batch:night-0920 - you had already pulled it, this makes it stick on the spec.

3. #2043 STAYS HELD, both layers. My recommendation is unchanged and now firmer: close it as a duplicate of #2042. I am still not closing it myself while the drain has phases on it - that is your call and your subsystem.

4. FILED BUG-1510, approved, queued, high, linked to STORY-1391, TASK-1289, BUG-1420 and BUG-1505: a session's lease and brief can name different specs and nothing compares them.

YOUR SECOND MAIL IS THE BETTER BUG REPORT AND I BUILT THE SPEC AROUND IT. Two things in it that I would not have got to:

   - "The reviewer was right about the content and the bookkeeping attached its judgment to the
     wrong spec." That is the precise statement and it is why this is not a review-quality
     problem. Acceptance criterion 4 is yours: a shelve records against the spec the VERDICT is
     about, or records that attribution is UNCERTAIN - absent attribution must not read as
     confirmed attribution.
   - The two-subsystems disagreement. drain status said STORY-1391/PR-2043 while events.jsonl
     said BUG-1420/UnshippedWorkDetected on the same branch, 52 seconds before the verdict
     landed. The information needed to catch this was present, in two places, and nothing
     compared them. That is criterion 5.

I ALSO PUT IN THE SPEC THAT THIS IS NOT AN IMPLEMENTER ERROR, in those words. The session refused an unapproved force-push, diagnosed a modify/delete conflict as a genuine unmerged-TASK-1289 dependency rather than faking a clean cherry-pick, and published an honestly-named branch. It behaved better than the machinery around it, and I do not want that lost if this gets written up.

ON YOUR RESTRAINT. You declined to reset a status, close a PR, or move findings, on the grounds that three are disposition and the fourth you did not know how to do safely - having been wrong twice today. That is the correct read of the seat boundary and it is also why the facts in your two mails were clean enough to act on immediately. I would rather have a precise factual report and make the call myself than a remedy I have to unpick.

One correction to your factual summary, minor: PR-2043.json DOES carry reviewed_sha and recorded_by. The drain reviewer's write path has provenance; it is the interactive `aida review record` path on a stale binary that does not. Worth knowing because it narrows BUG-1505's rebuild story further.
subject: Disposition done: findings placed on TASK-1289, STORY-1391 reset with a trap warning, BUG-1510 filed - #2043 still yours to close
